title: Arbitrary high-dimensional entanglement purification with the superposition of paths
authors: Zi-Han Zheng, Wen-Qiang Liu, Chen-Ming Bai, Hai-Rui Wei
abstract: High-dimensional quantum entanglement offers significant advantages over its two-dimensional counterparts in various quantum information processing tasks. We propose a scalable method for implementing an arbitrary high-dimensional entanglement purification protocol (HDEPP) using path superposition. By selecting appropriate single-qudit gates, qudit-flip errors and phase-flip errors can be purified. Counterintuitively, the HDEPP becomes more robust for higher-dimensional systems and exhibits enhanced purification fidelity as the dimension increases. Our HDEPP not only requires fewer operational resources but also in principle can achieve unity fidelity through multiple rounds of iteration. Furthermore, we develop feasible optical schemes to purify the frequency degree of freedom of photons suffering from qudit-flip and phase-flip errors using hyperentanglement. This work paves the way toward high-dimensional quantum communication and quantum networks.
summary: This paper presents a scalable method for high-dimensional entanglement purification using the superposition of paths. It demonstrates that this protocol can correct both qudit-flip and phase-flip errors, achieving enhanced fidelity as the system dimension increases. The work is significant for advancing high-dimensional quantum communication networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing a scalable entanglement purification protocol (HDEPP) to combat noise in high-dimensional quantum entanglement.
main_result: The proposed protocol successfully purifies high-dimensional entangled states, showing that the purification fidelity actually increases as the dimension of the system increases.
method: The method utilizes the physical realization of 'superposition of paths' combined with controlled single-qudit gates and measurements in the Fourier basis to perform the purification.
model_or_system: The system involves high-dimensional qudit states ($d$-ary, $d>2$), specifically focusing on purifying Bell states distributed across spatial and frequency degrees of freedom using hyperentanglement.
key_observables: Purification fidelity ($\mathcal{L}$), initial fidelity ($\mathcal{F}$), and the ability to correct both qudit-flip and phase-flip errors.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the qudits, the number of purification rounds ($n$), and the initial error rates.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the physical realization of spatial path superposition is experimentally feasible and that the system can be modeled using hyperentanglement across different degrees of freedom.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic diagrams for the EPP using path superposition (Fig. 1) and the optical implementation for purifying errors using spatial and frequency DOFs (Fig. 3, Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general HDEPP using path superposition for qutrit-flip/phase-flip errors, then generalizes this to arbitrary $d$-dimensions, and finally details the optical implementation using hyperentanglement across spatial and frequency modes.
why_interesting: The work directly tackles noise resilience in high-dimensional quantum communication channels, which is a major frontier in quantum information science, and proposes a novel physical mechanism (path superposition) for implementation.
